questions.stem: What is the primary general principle regarding antimicrobial administration when collecting microbiological clinical specimens?
options: Collect the specimen after at least 48 hours of empirical broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy
Collect the specimen before administering antimicrobial agents whenever possible
Administer a single prophylactic dose of penicillin immediately before taking the sample
Antimicrobial timing has no impact on the diagnostic yield of bacterial cultures
questions.explanation: Collecting specimens prior to initiating antimicrobial therapy prevents suppression of pathogen growth and minimizes false-negative culture results.

questions.stem: Which bacterial pathogen is explicitly highlighted as cold-sensitive, meaning its stool specimen must NOT be refrigerated even during transport delays greater than 2 hours?
options: Clostridioides difficile toxin
Yersinia enterocolitica
Shigella species
Escherichia coli O157:H7
questions.explanation: While refrigeration at 4°C is generally used for delayed specimens (>2 hours), Shigella is cold-sensitive and can be killed by refrigeration without transport medium. C. difficile toxin is also an exception because freeze-thaw cycles destroy the toxin, whereas Yersinia utilizes cold enrichment.

questions.stem: Charcoal is added to transport media (such as Amies or Stuart with charcoal) primarily to improve the survival of which category of microorganisms?
options: Obligate intracellular viruses
Fastidious organisms (e.g., Neisseria , Bordetella , Campylobacter , Haemophilus )
Spore-forming anaerobic bacilli
Non-pathogenic indigenous skin flora
questions.explanation: Charcoal neutralizes toxic fatty acids and metabolic substances, enhancing the survival of fastidious organisms that have complex or specific nutritional and environmental requirements.

questions.stem: According to universal sample safety considerations, how should high-risk specimens such as suspected Tuberculosis sputum or Cholera fecal samples be transported to the laboratory?
options: Hand-carried in unsealed open glass tubes without paperwork
In plastic sealable bags with a separate pouch for requisition orders, clearly labeled as high risk
Submerged in 10% neutral buffered formalin
Packed in dry ice inside an airtight wooden box
questions.explanation: Safety guidelines mandate treating all specimens as biohazardous, using barrier protection, placing specimens in sealable plastic bags with a separate pouch for paperwork to prevent external container contamination, and clearly labeling high-risk specimens.

questions.stem: What is the proper procedure for collecting a diagnostic sputum sample for lower respiratory tract culture?
options: Collect 10 mL of clear, foamy oral saliva after eating
Rinse mouth with clear water, take deep breaths, and cough up deep bronchial sputum (≥1 mL) into a sterile container prior to antibiotics
Perform a superficial swab of the anterior tongue surface
Swab the submandibular salivary gland duct
questions.explanation: Expectorated sputum must originate from deep coughing (avoiding salivary contamination), measure at least 1 mL, and be collected into a sterile container before antibiotic administration. Clear and foamy samples represent saliva and are non-diagnostic.

questions.stem: Which of the following specimens must be processed in the microbiology laboratory within 2 hours of collection due to pathogen fragility?
options: Tissue biopsy for mycobacteria
Middle ear fluid and sputum (if Streptococcus pneumoniae is suspected)
Routine urine for boric acid preservation
Environmental water sample for chemical analysis
questions.explanation: Middle ear fluid, sputum (if S. pneumoniae is suspected), bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), and Legionella cultures must be processed within 2 hours of collection to ensure organism viability.

questions.stem: What is the recommended transport medium for stool specimens delayed for more than 2 hours to maintain the viability of enteric pathogens like Salmonella , Shigella , and Campylobacter ?
options: Alkaline peptone water
Cary-Blair transport medium
Guanidine thiocyanate PCR buffer
Michel's fixative solution
questions.explanation: Stool samples delayed >2 hours should be placed in Cary-Blair transport medium, which maintains the viability of enteric pathogens such as Salmonella , Shigella , Campylobacter , and Vibrio .

questions.stem: When collecting a stool sample from a patient with suspected Campylobacter jejuni gastroenteritis, which specific environmental condition and medium are required?
options: Anaerobic jar at 4°C in saline
Microaerophilic conditions using a charcoal transport medium (without refrigeration)
Aerobic broth containing 10% formalin
Cold enrichment at 4°C for 4 weeks in boric acid
questions.explanation: C. jejuni requires microaerophilic conditions and charcoal-containing transport medium. It is listed under organisms that should NOT be refrigerated.

questions.stem: What type of specimen is required for diagnosing Clostridioides difficile antibiotic-associated diarrhea, and what collection method is strictly prohibited?
options: Solid formed stool; cotton swabs are mandatory
Liquid or unformed stool in a sterile container; swabs must NOT be used
Rectal swab in Cary-Blair medium; liquid stool is rejected
Gastric aspirate in sodium hydroxide
questions.explanation: C. difficile testing requires unformed or liquid stool collected in a sterile container (and refrigerated at 4°C if delayed). Formed stool and swabs are inappropriate and rejected.

questions.stem: What specialized technique can be used to enhance the laboratory recovery of Yersinia enterocolitica from stool specimens?
options: Incubation at 42°C for 48 hours
Cold enrichment by storing the specimen at 4°C for 2 to 4 weeks
Boiling the stool sample in peptone water for 10 minutes
Adding high concentrations of penicillin to the transport tube
questions.explanation: Yersinia enterocolitica tolerates and multiplies at cold temperatures; cold enrichment at 4°C for 2–4 weeks enhances its recovery over other fecal flora.

questions.stem: Which urinary specimen collection method is considered the sterile "gold standard" for obtaining completely uncontaminated bladder urine in infants?
options: Pediatric adhesive bag urine
Midstream clean-catch urine
Suprapubic Aspirate (SPA)
Foley catheter drainage bag aspirate
questions.explanation: Suprapubic aspiration involves inserting a needle percutaneously through the lower abdominal wall directly into the bladder, bypassing urethral flora to obtain a completely sterile sample.

questions.stem: If a midstream clean-catch urine sample cannot be delivered to the laboratory within 30 minutes, what preservative tube should be used to prevent bacterial overgrowth?
options: Sodium citrate tube (blue-top)
Boric acid preservative tube (grey-top)
EDTA tube (purple-top)
Heparinized blood tube (green-top)
questions.explanation: Boric acid preservative tubes (grey-top) inhibit bacterial overgrowth while allowing culture viability if urine transport is delayed beyond 30 minutes.

questions.stem: Why are nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT / PCR) specimens for Chlamydia trachomatis or Mycoplasma genitalium collected in liquid-based NAAT transport tubes rather than standard Amies charcoal swabs?
options: NAAT transport tubes contain guanidine thiocyanate buffers that lyse cells, inactivate nucleases (DNase/RNase), and stabilize DNA/RNA
Amies charcoal transport medium destroys bacterial DNA within 5 minutes
NAAT tubes maintain live bacterial motility for darkfield microscopy
NAAT tubes allow simultaneous aerobic bacterial culture growth
questions.explanation: NAAT transport tubes contain specialized lysis buffers (e.g., guanidine thiocyanate) that lyse cells, neutralize destructive nucleases (DNases/RNases), and preserve target nucleic acids for PCR testing.

questions.stem: What is a critical transport temperature rule for clinical specimens suspected of containing Neisseria gonorrhoeae ?
options: Freeze immediately at -20°C
Store at room temperature and do NOT refrigerate, as N. gonorrhoeae is sensitive to cold
Incubate at 4°C in a cold enrichment broth for 14 days
Keep on wet ice for 48 hours
questions.explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is fragile and cold-sensitive. Genital or eye specimens for gonococcal culture must be kept at room temperature and plated promptly (within 6 hours if using transport medium).

questions.stem: How must Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) collected via lumbar puncture for suspected bacterial meningitis be handled and transported?
options: Refrigerate immediately at 4°C to prevent leukocyte autolysis
Transport to the lab immediately within 15–30 minutes at room temperature (35–37°C); do NOT refrigerate
Freeze at -80°C in a glycerol bath
Mix with an equal volume of 70% ethanol
questions.explanation: Fastidious neuro-pathogens like Neisseria meningitidis and Haemophilus influenzae are killed by cold. CSF must be kept at room temperature (or 35–37°C) and transported immediately within 15–30 minutes.

questions.stem: What is the recommended handling procedure for a corneal scraping specimen obtained from a patient with suspected bacterial or fungal keratitis?
options: Store in a refrigerator at 4°C for up to 48 hours
Process within 15–30 minutes at room temperature (do NOT refrigerate)
Immerse in formalin solution for 2 hours
Freeze immediately at -20°C
questions.explanation: Corneal scrapings dry out quickly and cold temperatures can kill fungi and delicate bacteria. They must be kept at room temperature and processed within 15–30 minutes.

questions.stem: In a patient with endophthalmitis, how should a small-volume vitreous aspirate (0.1–0.2 mL) be handled if transport to the laboratory will be delayed for more than 1 hour?
options: Store in a household refrigerator at 4°C
Inoculate directly into blood culture bottles (aerobic + anaerobic) and hold at 37°C in an incubator
Dilute with 10 mL of sterile tap water
Apply to a dry paper strip at room temperature
questions.explanation: Endophthalmitis vitreous aspirates are emergency samples of tiny volume (0.1–0.2 mL). If transport is delayed >1 hour, the aspirate should be inoculated directly into blood culture bottles and stored in a 37°C incubator.

questions.stem: What is the diagnostic GOLD STANDARD specimen for investigating a deep wound or surgical site infection?
options: Superficial wound swab of intact surrounding skin
Tissue biopsy or direct aspirate of pus
Saline rinse of the outer dressing
Dry cotton swab of the superficial wound margin
questions.explanation: Tissue biopsy or direct needle aspirate of pus is the gold standard for wound infections. Swabs are acceptable only for superficial wounds when tissue/aspirate is not feasible, because swabs often capture superficial colonizing skin microbiota.

questions.stem: Why must wound swab samples submitted for anaerobic bacterial culture NEVER be refrigerated?
options: Cold temperatures stimulate rapid fungal overgrowth
Cold kills anaerobes and fastidious bacteria
Refrigeration inactivates liquid Amies transport media
Cold causes immediate lysis of human red blood cells
questions.explanation: Wound swabs must be kept at room temperature (20–26°C) and delivered within 2 hours. Refrigeration is strictly avoided because cold kills fastidious anaerobes (e.g., Bacteroides , Peptostreptococcus , Clostridium ).

questions.stem: What documentation process creates an unbroken paper trail tracking every individual who handles a clinical sample from collection to final disposal, ensuring legal defensibility?
options: Institutional Review Board (IRB) Approval
Chain of Custody
Antibiogram Surveillance
Universal Precautions Audit
questions.explanation: The Chain of Custody documents every person who handles a sample from collection to disposal, creating a paper trail crucial for legal defensibility and traceability.
